detail.title: Robustness and Redundancy in Quantum and Classical Records
detail.summary: Robustness in physical records is achieved when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom, enabling independent observers to reach consensus. This process, formalizable through Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and quantum Darwinism, effectively 'broadcasts' information. Furthermore, thermodynamic constraints, specifically the energy cost of erasing information (Landauer's principle), bound the long-term stability of these records in both classical and quantum substrates.
detail.reason: Notebook revision required to integrate thermodynamic constraints on record stability with existing redundancy frameworks.

detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers
detail.summary: Physical record robustness is an emergent property grounded in the proliferation of pointer states via decoherence into the environment, formalizable through Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS). Independent observers achieve consensus when the environment acts as a redundant broadcasting channel, effectively amplifying information without disturbing the system record. Recent analysis confirms that objectivity is contingent upon the capacity of the environment to encode sufficient redundancy, allowing local, independent measurements to align.
detail.reason: Revising findings to incorporate refined understanding of objective character in macroscopic transitions as supported by recent peer evidence.

detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records
detail.summary: Robustness occurs when multiple independent observers arrive at consistent records of system states. This consistency is secured by the stability of einselected states which minimize decoherence and environmental noise.
